evals.prompt: I have the cs-resources template and 5 clips in ~/Downloads (hook.mov, resource1.mov, resource2.mov, resource3.mov, cta.mov) plus a music track. Can you edit them into that format for me?
evals.expected_output: Should read formats/cs-resources.json to see its blocks/slots, probe and thumbnail each candidate clip, match them to slots using slot instructions, confirm the planned mapping with the user before writing job.json, copy files into jobs/<name>/assets/, write job.json, run npm run pipeline -- --job jobs/<name>, read gates.json, run the self-check (timeline-view.sh at cut boundaries from edl.json) before handing over out/<name>.mp4, and report any gate failures or self-check findings honestly.
assertions: Reads the target format's blocks/slots before matching footage
Confirms the slot mapping with the user before writing job.json
Writes job.json with correct relative asset paths
Runs npm run pipeline against the job
Reads gates.json rather than assuming success from exit code alone
Runs a self-check using timeline-view.sh at real cut boundaries from edl.json
Delivers the output path plus an honest status, not just 'done'

evals.prompt: the render finished but there's a weird flash right where it cuts to the second resource clip
evals.expected_output: Should locate the relevant cut boundary in artifacts/<job>/edl.json, run timeline-view.sh around that boundary to inspect it, form a hypothesis about the cause (e.g. a transition mismatch, a trim boundary issue), apply the smallest fix (e.g. --only assemble or --only render, or an overrides entry), re-render, and re-check with timeline-view.sh before declaring it fixed — not just re-render blindly and assume it's resolved.
assertions: Locates the specific cut in edl.json rather than re-rendering blindly
Uses timeline-view.sh to inspect the boundary before and after the fix
Applies a targeted fix (--only stage or an overrides entry) rather than a full re-author
Verifies the fix before telling the user it's resolved
